display.title: Episode 178: The Shpoler Zeide's Dance (Isru Chag Shavuos)
display.summary_short: On Isru Chag Shavuos Uncle Yossi recalls the Yom Tov, then tells how Eliyahu HaNavi taught the Shpoler Zeide to dance to free a prisoner, and teaches about the mezuzah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Isru Chag, the day after Shavuos 5745. Uncle Yossi looks back at the Yom Tov: hearing the Aseres HaDibros, flowers recalling the green slopes of Har Sinai, staying up for the Tikkun, and eating dairy foods. He explains that Isru Chag 'ties' one more day to the festival so its resolutions carry on all year. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a yeshiva boy recites the Shema and tells how he is getting friends to buy letters in a new Sefer Torah. Story time: Rabbi Avraham HaMalach asks the Shpoler Zeide who taught him to dance so well. The answer is Eliyahu HaNavi. A cruel poritz made Jewish debtors dance in a bearskin and threw the losers to his dogs. The Shpoler Zeide took a prisoner's place, outdanced the poritz and walked out free. Rabbi Avraham says such dancing may be higher than his own prayers. Mitzvah Time introduces a new call-in quiz and teaches that the mitzvah of mezuzah appears twice in Devarim, in chapters 6 and 11.
display.lesson: Carry the spirit of Yom Tov into every day, and use every talent Hashem gives you to help another Jew.

date.note: 'Just a day after Shavuos... Isru Chag, which is today'; Shavuos 5745 was 26-27 May. Weekly estimate was 3 weeks late.

advisories.note: A cruel poritz jails Jews who cannot pay rent and humiliates them.
Prisoners who lose the dance are thrown to hungry dogs; the hero escapes unharmed.
The hero gives a guard whiskey so he falls asleep.

sources_cited.note: The two places the mitzvah of mezuzah is written.
